actions: switched to Hypno  // Jynx with a sash is a Lovely Kiss lead, and Trick Room moves at -7 priority — Slowbro would be asleep before the room ever went up. Hypno has Insomnia. I trade one turn to make their lead illegal.
Jynx used Lovely Kiss  // Slowbro is the Trick Room button. The Apothecary does not let a button get pressed — Lovely Kiss puts the setter to sleep before the room ever exists.

Hypno used Trick Room  // Their sleep move just failed into my sleep-immune setter. That is the safest window I will ever get to put the room up — take it before Jynx swaps to something that actually threatens Hypno.
switched to Zapdos  // Insomnia walls my Kiss, so Jynx has no business here. Zapdos comes in to absorb the five Trick Room turns and start writing prescriptions — Toxic doesn't care how fast you are.

switched to Rhydon  // Zapdos into Lightning Rod is a free door. Rhydon is immune to their electric STAB, and inside the room a 252-Atk Stone Edge hits Zapdos before it ever moves. Spend a room turn buying the right attacker.
Zapdos used Toxic  // The room has five turns; Toxic has all of them. Badly poisoned is the one clock that ticks faster the longer they stall.

lines.text: Rhydon is hurt by its toxic! (-13)

actions: Rhydon used Stone Edge  // Toxic put Rhydon on a timer, so Rhydon spends itself now. Stone Edge is doubly effective on Zapdos, moves first inside the room, and makes no contact — Static gets no say. 80% accuracy is the only thing between me and a free kill.

switched to Arbok  // Rhydon is already on the toxic clock, so Zapdos has no medicine left for it. Arbok walks in, Intimidate cuts the dose of that 130 base Attack in half, and Earthquake answers rock with earth.

lines.text: Rhydon is hurt by its toxic! (-26)

actions: Rhydon used Earthquake  // Intimidate and a missed Edge cost me a room turn, but Arbok walked into the wrong matchup: Earthquake is 2x on poison and its own Gunk Shot is quartered by ground/rock. Rhydon is dying to toxic regardless — cash it in for a body.
Arbok used Earthquake  // Rhydon is poisoned, so Glare has nothing left to give it and Venoshock is walled by rock. Earthquake is simply the correct dose.

lines.text: Rhydon is hurt by its toxic! (-39)

actions: switched to Jynx  // Rhydon hits like a truck but its Special Defense is base 45. Focus Sash guarantees Jynx lives exactly one Earthquake, and one Ice Beam is all the prescription she needs.

Rhydon used Megahorn  // Last turn of the room, so it has to hurt. Rhydon being already poisoned means Lovely Kiss is dead text — Jynx can't sleep something that's already sick. Megahorn is 2x on its psychic half at the best accuracy I've got; leave Jynx a husk for whatever walks in next.
Jynx used Ice Beam  // Ice Beam into a base-45 Special Defense, with the toxic already down 78. The sash pays for the privilege of going second in the room.

lines.text: Jynx hung on with its Focus Sash!
The twisted dimensions returned to normal!

actions: switched to Hypno  // Jynx is on 1 HP with its sash burned. Hypno is the one body it can't answer — Insomnia blanks Lovely Kiss and 252 SpDef eats Ice Beam — and it's carrying the second room. Anything Hypno touches now kills.

Hypno used Trick Room  // Hitting a 1% Jynx now doesn't save me — it still moves before Hypno this turn. The room does. Twist the dimensions and Jynx never gets another Lovely Kiss off, because next turn my 'slowest' Pokémon acts first and finishes it. Hypno is at full HP and immune to their lead: this is a free setup turn.

Jynx used Ice Beam  // Insomnia means no Kiss and Psychic is resisted, so Ice Beam is the only honest damage. Jynx is on 1 HP anyway — spend her last breath on the Trick Room setter and she buys me a free switch when she goes.

Hypno used Psychic  // The room flips the order and Hypno moves first for once. Psychic kills the 1% Jynx outright, and if they pivot instead, Psychic is 2x into the poison types a status team is made of. Sleep never gets another chance.

switched to Zapdos  // Under the room Jynx moves last and dies for nothing, so I bank her — 1 HP of Lovely Kiss is still worth more than a corpse. Zapdos is Ground-immune and bulky enough to be the ward that outlasts the room.

switched to Machamp  // Three room turns left and Hypno hits like a pillow — swap to the hammer while the dimensions are still twisted. No Guard means Stone Edge is a 100%-accurate 2x into Zapdos, no 80% dice like the one that cost me Rhydon. Machamp's Assault Vest handles whatever Zapdos throws on the way in.

Zapdos used Toxic  // Hypno is the room's architect and Insomnia makes it immune to my Kiss — so it gets the other prescription. Toxic on a wall that plans to sit there all game is the best trade in the sport.

lines.text: Machamp is hurt by its toxic! (-12)

actions: Machamp used Stone Edge  // Two room turns left and Machamp is on a toxic clock, so every point of damage has to land. No Guard makes Stone Edge a 100% 2x on Zapdos and it's non-contact, so Static can't paralyze me on the way through. No dice this time.

Zapdos used Discharge  // Assault Vest means Machamp is a pure attacker on a death clock with no way to heal off my Toxic. Zapdos resists its Fighting STAB, so I just add Discharge to the bill and let the poison compound.

lines.text: Machamp is hurt by its toxic! (-24)

actions: Machamp used Stone Edge  // Last turn of the room, and the arithmetic is clean: Stone Edge hit for 105, Zapdos is sitting on 78. No Guard means there is no miss to hope for. The room closes with a body on the floor.

switched to Golbat  // Zapdos is one Stone Edge from the slab, so Golbat takes over: it quarters Fighting, and once Roost strips its Flying type the Stone Edges stop being super effective too. Machamp is already 30% down the toxic drain — I just have to outlive the last turn of the room.

lines.text: Golbat restored a little HP (Sitrus Berry, +45).
Machamp is hurt by its toxic! (-36)
The twisted dimensions returned to normal!

actions: Machamp used Stone Edge  // Outside the room I move dead last, on purpose — and Machamp's toxic counter says it has two turns left regardless. So spend them. Stone Edge already did 127 to Golbat and its Sitrus is eaten; it's sitting around 100. If Machamp survives the turn, Golbat doesn't.

Golbat used Roost  // Outside the room I move first, so Roost lands before Stone Edge — and a Roosted Golbat is pure Poison, which takes rock neutrally and Fighting at half. Machamp's toxic is at 48 a turn now; it dies of my medicine, not my fists.

lines.text: Machamp is hurt by its toxic! (-49)

actions: switched to Muk  // Machamp's next toxic tick is -60 off 31 HP — staying in donates a body for a coinflip against a Roost staller. Pull it instead and send the one Pokémon The Apothecary cannot write on: Muk is poison-type, so Toxic, Sludge Bomb and Venoshock are all dead letters, and Ice Punch out-damages Golbat's Roost.
Golbat used Air Slash  // The toxic would kill it at end of turn anyway, but Air Slash is 2x on Fighting and gets there first — no reason to donate Golbat another 60 HP to a corpse.

lines.text: Muk restored a little HP (Black Sludge, +13).

actions: Muk used Ice Punch  // The Apothecary's whole gimmick needs a patient to write on, and Muk refuses the prescription — poison-typed, so Toxic and Venoshock are blanks, and Black Sludge pays back half of Air Slash. Ice Punch is 2x into Golbat and beats what Roost can restore. I out-attrition the attrition team.

Golbat used Confuse Ray  // Muk shrugs off poison, so I reach for a different bottle. Confusion is not a status condition — it stacks with a burn later — and a confused Muk swinging at its own face is the cheapest damage on the board.

lines.text: Muk hurt itself in its confusion! (-29)
Muk restored a little HP (Black Sludge, +13).
